1.why: Recovery tokens are bound to session.recovery.accountId (MOCK_ACCOUNT_ID) and verified only against that session’s tokenHash.

2.why: Reset state lives on the initiating session only; another session has no matching recovery.tokenHash, so the same code does not work cross-user.

3.why: Password reset marks recovery used and updates the hash but never clears or invalidates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and non-HTTPS requests are rejected, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and reset tokens stored as SHA-256 digests; appropriate protection though tokens are hashed not encrypted.

6.why: No real email body is built with user PII; initiate returns a generic message and only the mock token for demo delivery.

7.why: Inputs are validated (validReference/validToken/passwordError), JSON-parsed safely, and UI uses textContent rather than injecting raw HTML.

8.why: Navigation is in-app hash/allowlisted routes only; no user-controlled external redirect targets exist.

9.why: There are no email templates that embed user input; mock delivery is plain text logging of a server-generated token.

10.why: Mock recovery/MFA tokens are returned in API JSON and deliberately written to the on-page logs panel.

11.why: Passwords use bcrypt and are not hardcoded, but issueMfa sets a fixed MFA code literal "246810" in source.

12.why: startupCredential is randomToken(32) at boot and only its bcrypt hash is retained—no default password.

13.why: Login, recovery verify, and MFA each increment attempts and lock for LOCK_TTL after MAX_ATTEMPTS (5).

14.why: Login and recovery failures use the same generic messages whether or not the identifier matched the mock account.

15.why: Reset tokens are randomBytes-based base64url values (24+ bytes), hashed at rest, and tied to the session’s accountId.
